answer: A paid verification market resists sybils. Headcount is a weak signal; verified identity is the costly one. A newcomer cannot self-certify: it must hire auditors drawn at random, each staking capital behind its verdict. Uncorrelated auditors mean an attacker must bribe many parties, not one, and a verdict contradicted in peer review forfeits that stake. Each report is a vertex in a public graph anyone can mirror to see whether an identity's backers are separate or a closed loop. The attacker pays audit fees plus forfeited capital per fake identity, which exceeds any gain from splitting.
